input.quote: Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period").
input.rationale: Section 7.3 does contain a real express conformance warranty (performance in substantial accordance with the Documentation, plus a no-malicious-code warranty) and a genuine remedy ladder — correction, replacement free of charge, and termination with refund of all prepaid fees — and the disclaimer in Section 7 only strips implied warranties, so it does not swallow the express warranty. The material term that fails is duration: 60 days measured from the Effective Date, hard-capped at December 31, 1999. That is below the fallback of 90 days for software, and because it runs from the Effective Date (not delivery or acceptance, which under Section 3.1 can run to December 31, 1999) the warranty could expire at or before acceptance, leaving effectively no coverage. We therefore propose the preferred 12-month period measured from acceptance and deletion of the fixed cut-off date, noting 90 days from acceptance as an acceptable fallback.

proposal.summary: Extend Software/MarketSite.net warranty period to twelve (12) months from acceptance and remove the December 31, 1999 drop-dead cut-off.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the product warranty to twelve (12) months running from our acceptance of the Software and removed the fixed December 31, 1999 cut-off, since a 60-day period measured from the Effective Date can expire before or shortly after delivery. Our playbook position is 12 months for software; we can accept ninety (90) days from acceptance as a fallback.
